summary: You delivered a solid, well-justified coral-reef SSO mission for Australia. Introduction and main design comprehensively cover launch, orbit, ground station and EOL with STK evidence. Your Vega E from Guiana, 600 km SSO at 97.7924 deg, Mount Pleasant access, and drag-sail EOL are persuasive. Presentation limits your overall mark due to figure labelling and referencing.
next_steps: Add formal Figure numbers, titles and in-text callouts for all STK views (e.g. Image 4 12h-apart view) and access reports, to move presentation to Accomplished.
Replace Wikipedia timeline citations in Launch and Bibliography with proper aerospace sources (ESA, industry) and format references with author/date and proper in-text citation.
In Conclusion, add quantitative summary from your Orbit and Ground Control & Communications results (revisit, coverage %, deorbit delta-v/time) to strengthen evidence-based closure.

criteria.C1: You did well in Introduction: primary mission (fluid-lensing coral/ocean monitoring), rationale (bleaching/acidification), single-satellite justification, and users CSIRO/BOM/university/gov clearly addressed. For Accomplished upper band, add more literature on stakeholder needs and explicit number trade-off.
criteria.C2: Strong coverage: Vega E from Guiana Space Centre, 600 km SSO with 97.7924° inclination calculation, direct injection, Mount Pleasant access, 5-year life and drag-sail EOL – all supported by STK 3D views and reports. To improve, justify inclination source and refine circular-orbit elements (set ω=0, use true longitude).
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion synthesises Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications and EOL from evidence and acknowledges Vega E risk with Vega C alternative. For higher Accomplished, make it more quantitative – summarise key performance numbers from your design.
criteria.C4: Report has logical structure and readable executive summary. To reach Accomplished, use consistent Figure numbering/titles instead of informal captions like 'STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart', and replace bare Wikipedia URLs in Bibliography with properly cited authoritative sources.
